answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a cedar-anchored reputation grove. Each identity must grow one cedar root by doing verified, useful work over time, so a cheap copy cannot instantly claim standing. Trust then spreads like yarrow: a rotating quorum of unrelated witnesses must independently confirm that work before any privilege is granted, blocking a single clique from minting fake peers. A lotus bloom cooldown then gates rewards: new identities mature slowly, and fraud in that window wilts the lineage, wiping its credit. Copies thus become costly, slow, and easy to prune.
